source_caption_text:
Everyone BUT Eminem is in the selfie 😭😂🤳

Happy 54th birthday to Eminem 🎂🐐 From Detroit’s battle rap scene to worldwide recognition, Marshall Mathers built a career that helped introduce generations of listeners to hip-hop.

His breakthrough with The Slim Shady LP in 1999 brought his sharp wordplay, outrageous humor and unmistakable delivery to a much bigger audience. The album earned him his first two GRAMMYs in 2000, winning Best Rap Album and Best Rap Solo Performance for “My Name Is.” His career has since grown to include 15 GRAMMY wins. 🏆 (grammy.com)

The Marshall Mathers LP and The Eminem Show followed with songs that remain central to his catalog. From the storytelling on “Stan” to the personal reflections on “Cleanin’ Out My Closet,” Eminem gave listeners much more than technical ability. His songs could be funny, uncomfortable, vulnerable and confrontational sometimes within the same verse.

His success also reached the big screen through 8 Mile. “Lose Yourself” became his first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and made history as the first rap song to win the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 2003. Nearly two decades later, he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as part of its 2022 class. (rockhall.com, oscars.org, eminem.com)

Across different eras, his ability to bend words, build intricate rhyme schemes and turn personal experiences into memorable records has kept fans listening closely. Whether you discovered him through “Without Me,” “Mockingbird,” “Not Afraid” or “Rap God,” there’s a different chapter of his career that means something to you.

Show some birthday love to Eminem ❤️🔥 Which song made you a fan?
